title: Sir Ralph Boswell to his cousin William Boswell, Dec 1627 / Jan 1628, TNA SP 106/5 (DECODE R413; catalogued as King Charles I to Boswell)

documents.date: probably 15 Dec 1627 or shortly after; endorsed received 24 Jan 1627/8
documents.route: Sir Ralph Boswell (England) to William Boswell (abroad)

plaintext.source: Mark Woodard (Furman University), decipherment uploaded to DECODE R413, 2021-11-09

transcription.source: Woodard's letter transcription (a-x) in his DECODE PDF, checked against the DECODE images
transcription.notes: Ten numbered lines, no word division. Page 2 carries a contemporary sign-by-line tally (each sign with the line numbers it occurs in) and the endorsement 'Sr Ra: Boswele. 24 Jan. 1627'.

system.summary: Monoalphabetic substitution with invented graphic signs, one sign per letter, 24 signs seen; no word division; one or two signs possibly word codes.
system.notes: u/v one sign; P and F share or confuse (OFINION = opinion), H for F in HEARES (= feares).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R413 with the shared cookie: two page images and two PDFs, a 'cryptanalysis' and a 'key'.
The cryptanalysis PDF is Mark Woodard's 2021 decipherment (CrypTool 2 monoalphabetic analyzer): an English newsletter on Buckingham's return from Plymouth, three signs left as '?'.
Aligned Woodard's 442-letter transcription with his plaintext: each of 21 transcription letters maps to one plaintext letter without exception (l = B once reads O, a slip for R in LOLDES).
Resolved his gaps from context: p = S (HI[S] OWNE; OUR[S]), second w = a code or abbreviation for 'part' (FOR THE MOST [PART] ARE). The pair w x after 'conceaued he' stays unread.

Read the endorsement on p. 2 as 'Sr Ra: Boswele. 24 Jan. 1627': the sender is Sir Ralph Boswell, a kinsman ('my ... Cosin'), not Charles I. Saturday the 15th falls (Julian) in Dec 1627 or Mar 1628; with receipt on 24 Jan 1627/8 the letter's day is 15 Dec 1627.

outcome.method_basis: Mark Woodard's 2021 key and transcription on DECODE R413 were on the record before the attempt; the project filled the signs he left open.
outcome.notes: Solved by Woodard 2021. Added here: the gap readings, the sender (Sir Ralph Boswell, not the King) and the date from the endorsement. Catalogue entry 63 removed.
